target: Let u be a complex number that is not algebraic (so transcendental over Q̄), with ρ = uū algebraic, so ū = ρ/u. Let a₁ ≠ a₂ be non-zero algebraic numbers, z_i = u/(u² − a_i), H₀ = Q̄ + Q̄u + Q̄ū and W = H₀ + Q̄z₁ + Q̄z₂, a 5-dimensional Q̄-space of rational functions of u. Claim (a): there are Q̄-independent x₁, x₂ and Q̄-independent y₁, y₂, y₃ in ℂ with all six products x_i y_j in W. Claim (b): for every w in W outside H₀, the 4-dimensional space H₀ + Q̄w contains no such 2 × 3 product family. Nothing is assumed about z₁, z₂ being conjugate. So the pair of poles produces a 2 × 3 configuration that cannot be seen by adjoining any single element to H₀.

leads.citation: C. Bachoc, O. Serra, G. Zémor, An analogue of Vosper's theorem for extension fields, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 163 (2017), 423-452; arXiv:1501.00602v2. DOI 10.1017/S0305004117000044.
leads.location: Theorem 33 (section 7, arXiv v2 pp. 25-26), with Theorem 2 (p. 2). Journal numbering not checked.
leads.quote: Let F be an algebraically closed field and let L/F be a non-trivial extension
leads.derivation: The translation is mine; the paper never mentions this setting, and Theorem 33 yields claim (b) only. Take F = Q̄, L = ℂ. Suppose X, Y have dimensions 2, 3 and XY ⊂ T = H₀ + Q̄w. T is 4-dimensional, so Theorem 2 gives dim XY = 4 = 2 + 3 − 1 and XY = T. Theorem 33 gives X = g⟨1,a⟩, Y = g′⟨1,a,a²⟩, so T = s⟨1,a,a²,a³⟩ with s = gg′. Then a is a ratio of elements of T, so a ∈ Q̄(u). Since 1, u ∈ T, u is a ratio of two cubics in a, so u ∈ Q̄(a). Hence Q̄(a) = Q̄(u), a is Möbius in u, and 1 = sP(a) with deg P ≤ 3. So all of T = {R(a)/P(a)} has at most 3 distinct poles on P¹. But u, 1/u and w give poles at ∞, 0 and ±√a_i for some i with non-zero coefficient: at least 4 points. Contradiction. Claim (a) is a direct identity: x = (1, u⁻²), y = (u, z₁, z₂), using z_i/u² = (z_i − 1/u)/a_i and 1/u = ū/ρ.

leads.citation: C. Bachoc, A. Couvreur, G. Zémor, Towards a function field version of Freiman's theorem, Algebraic Combinatorics 1 (2018), no. 4, 501-521. DOI 10.5802/alco.19.
leads.location: Introduction (linear Vosper over algebraically closed K); Theorem 5.3; Theorem 6.1 (Mumford's product formula for Riemann-Roch spaces).
leads.quote: a linear version of Vosper's Theorem can be derived from an addition theorem
leads.derivation: Reaches only the existence half. In t = u², Theorem 6.1 with g = 0 gives L((0))·L((a₁)+(a₂)) = L((0)+(a₁)+(a₂)), and multiplying by u gives the configuration of claim (a). Its Vosper statement, Theorem 5.3, is symmetric (S² only), so it does not give claim (b), which needs the unsymmetric 2 × 3 case. For (b) use Bachoc-Serra-Zémor.

leads.citation: G. Diaz, Produits et quotients de combinaisons linéaires de logarithmes de nombres algébriques : conjectures et résultats partiels, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 19 (2007). DOI 10.5802/jtnb.592.
leads.location: Corollaire 5(4), p. 384; Théorème 7(2), p. 390 (page inferred from running heads).
leads.quote: Soient u ∈ C\Q et v ∈ C\{0}
leads.derivation: Corollaire 5(4) excludes {1/λ, 1/(λ+α)} from ℒ̃ using a 2 × 3 family with two poles, the same mechanism as claim (a), but with no invisibility statement and a different pair of functions. Théorème 7(2) excludes {v, vu, vu², vu³}, which by Bachoc-Serra-Zémor Theorem 33 is the shape of every 2 × 3 configuration in a 4-dimensional space. Diaz does not state that classification, nor anything about H₀ + Q̄w.

notes:
**Result.** No printed text states the entry, and the "not found" for the explicit statement survives. But the entry follows from a printed theorem by a short translation of my own, which fits its "routine" class.

**The lead.** Bachoc-Serra-Zémor, Theorem 33 with Theorem 2, gives the only non-trivial step. Over an algebraically closed base field, a pair S, T with dim ST = dim S + dim T − 1 and both dimensions at least 2 has bases in geometric progression.

- It applies directly with F = Q̄, L = ℂ.
- So every 2 × 3 configuration in a 4-dimensional space T has the form T = s⟨1,a,a²,a³⟩.
- If 1, u ∈ T ⊂ Q̄(u), then a is Möbius in u and T has at most 3 distinct poles on P¹.
- H₀ + Q̄w has at least 4: ∞, 0 and at least two of ±√a_i. That is claim (b). The case of w with a single pole is included.
- Claim (a) is the identity z_i/u² = (z_i − 1/u)/a_i with x = (1, u⁻²), y = (u, z₁, z₂). In t = u², this is L(D₁)L(D₂) = L(D₁+D₂) in genus 0.

**Independent check of the step used**, so a verifier need not trust the valuation proof. Let X = ⟨f,g⟩, r = g/f.

1. r ∉ Q̄, and Q̄ is algebraically closed, so r is transcendental and Y ≠ rY. Hence dim(Y + rY) ≥ 4.
2. Equality gives dim(Y ∩ rY) = 2. Put Y₁ = Y ∩ r⁻¹Y, of dimension 2.
3. Y₁ and rY₁ are 2-dimensional inside the 3-dimensional Y, so they share some t = rt′ with t′ ∈ Y₁, t ≠ 0.
4. Then t′, rt′, r²t′ ∈ Y and are independent, so Y = t′⟨1,r,r²⟩.

I did this by hand. sympy was not available, so nothing was machine-checked.

**Honest limits on "implies".**

- Theorem 33 does not mention poles, circles or H₀.
- The pole count and the reduction to Q̄(u) are my translation.
- Claim (a) does not come from Theorem 33; it is a one-line identity.
- The paper is already in the local library at sources/others/, though the entry's source line does not name it.
- The theorem is a 2017 statement in additive combinatorics, unconnected to the transcendence literature. A local grep found no Vosper, Kneser or Cauchy-Davenport mention in the Diaz or Roy folders, DALAG or ODP.
- Only a 2 × 3 case on a 4-dimensional space is used.

**Citation trail on the transcendence side.**

- OpenCitations lists two citers of Diaz 2004 (Diaz 2007, Butler) and none of Diaz 2007, though that index is thin for this journal.
- Roy 1992's citers are mostly p-adic regulator papers.
- zbMATH's 2026 listings under 11J81 were looked through (first 30 of 51), and 11J86 only cursorily (first 20 of 64). The only post-5 October items that surfaced on topic were Waldschmidt's strategy survey (arXiv:2610.39810), which has no relevant content, and Cano et al. (arXiv:2611.00456), which is unrelated.
- I found no new paper on Diaz's conjecture or on configurations in ℒ̃ after 5 October 2026.
- Diaz 2007 Cor. 5(4) and Th. 7(2) are the closest in spirit, and I record them as analogues. Cor. 5(4) shows the two-pole mechanism and Th. 7(2) the geometric shape, but neither has an invisibility statement.

**Citation trail on the additive-combinatorics side.**

- Of 36 OpenCitations citers of Bachoc-Serra-Zémor, I looked up 16 titles: nearly all concern finite-field coding or Sidon spaces, plus Wang-Tang. The other 20 are unchecked by title; those seen were finite-field work, away from algebraically closed bases.
- Bachoc-Couvreur-Zémor and Wessel treat the symmetric S² problem.

**Not settled.**

- Forward citations were incomplete: OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were both rate-limited, and OpenCitations and zbMATH have gaps for JTNB and for recent arXiv items. A later run with OpenAlex budget should repeat the citers of Diaz 2004 and 2007.
- I did not look for the classical algebraic-geometry form, where a 1-generic 2 × 3 matrix of linear forms in 4 variables gives a twisted cubic (Eisenbud's determinantal work, Hopf-Castelnuovo lemmas). It probably gives the same structural step with older attribution, but it is unverified and so is not listed as a lead.
- Journal page numbers for Theorem 33 are unconfirmed; I read arXiv v2.
- The OCR of Diaz 2007 drops the bar on Q̄. I read Q as Q̄ from context and did not check it against the page image.
